question: Saft batteries founded location history
markdown:
Saft, a French battery manufacturer, was founded in 1918 in Levallois-Perret by Victor Hérold, with roots tracing back to 1913. It became a subsidiary of TotalEnergies in 2016 and is the first French manufacturer of nickel and Li-ion batteries. The company operates globally with headquarters in France and has a significant plant in Valdosta, Georgia, which celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2025.
Saft was founded in Levallois-Perret, near Paris, France, in 1918 by Victor Hérold.
Saft was formally established as Société des Accumulateurs Fixes et de Traction (Saft) in Levallois-Perret in 1918.
Saft was listed partially on the Paris Bourse in 1924.
Saft was acquired by Compagnie Générale d'Électricité (CGE, later Alcatel) in 1928.
Saft expanded into alkaline and sintered-plate nickel batteries and moved production facilities to Poitiers between 1949 and the 1960s.
Saft was sold to Doughty Hanson & Co. in 2004.
Saft was acquired by TotalEnergies in 2016, becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary.
Saft operates globally with headquarters in France and manufacturing plants worldwide.
Saft was founded in 1913 as S.I.A.A. in Romainville, France.
Saft is the first French manufacturer of nickel and Li-ion batteries.
Saft's Valdosta plant in Georgia, USA, celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2025, having opened in 1975.
Saft's Valdosta plant is located on a 64-acre site on Gil Harbin Industrial Boulevard.
Saft's founder, Victor Hérold, was a disciple of Thomas Edison and involved in the battery industry as early as 1907.
Saft provides nickel and lithium-ion solutions for energy storage, telecommunications, marine, vehicles, aerospace, and defense.
